attribution.note: Marcus's own words in a footnote to his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The normalised text leaves out the neural-eval/symbolic-search detail, but the contract restores it. 'Several years' and 'leading' are kept.

contract.note: Marcus himself defines 'neurosymbolic' (neural evaluation plus symbolic search). Reading 'leading' as a top engine with major championship results is an ordinary reading. A window starting in 2020 is reasonable.

evidence.note: Official Stockfish 12 announcement (Sept 2020): NNUE neural evaluation became the default and feeds alpha-beta search. This is a project disclosure, but primary for its own architecture.
README pinned to version 17.1 (March 2025) confirms Stockfish still uses neural networks, shortly before the post.
Version-pinned search.cpp shows an explicit move loop with alpha-beta cutoffs, i.e. symbolic search.
Independent specialist blog reports Stockfish won the TCEC Season 27 superfinal (Jan 2025). This backs 'leading'; it is a secondary source, not the official record.

reviews.rationale: Dated official releases and pinned source code show neural evaluation combined with explicit alpha-beta search from Sept 2020 through March 2025, which covers several years before the June 2025 post. The TCEC S27 win backs leading status. No counterevidence in the packet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: A flat present-tense denial that proper world models emerge in LLMs. 'Proper' is undefined, and the scope (general LLMs or any sequence model) is unclear.

contract.note: Marcus never defines 'proper', and the contract supplies a coherence/updating/causal-use test. Whether specialised models like chess-trained GPTs count decides the result. The June 2025 window is an evaluator convention that pushes all the studies into background.

evidence.note: 2024 study: a chess-trained transformer learns board state that interventions can causally change. This cuts against an unrestricted denial, but the model is specialised, the study predates the window, and the representation is imperfect.
2024 study: program semantics emerge in a code LM in a synthetic grid world. This is positive evidence but narrow and outside the window.
2024 study: navigation transformers recover incoherent maps. This fits Marcus's skepticism but cannot show emergence never happens.

reviews.rationale: The evidence is all outside the window and pulls both ways: e7 and e8 show some causally used representations emerging in narrow models, while e9 shows incoherent ones. No source in the packet assesses general LLMs in June 2025. Whether the claim holds depends on how 'proper' and the scope are read, and the packet does not settle that.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: This is a firm assertion that hallucination risk exists in chatbots, not a hedge on Marcus's confidence. 'Risk' is part of what he claims, so the claim can be scored.

contract.note: The plain reading covers contemporary general-purpose generative chatbots, retrieval included. That is an ordinary reading. A universal reading over all possible future systems could not be tested, so the reading chosen decides the result.

evidence.note: OpenAI system card (April 2025, in window) reports large hallucination rates for o3 and o4-mini on its own benchmarks. This is a company disclosure, and benchmark rates are not conversation rates.

Google Research post (May 2025, in window) describes leftover hallucinations in retrieval-augmented systems across several vendors. It also reports mitigations, which limits it to showing persistent risk. Company disclosure.

reviews.rationale: Two sources dated inside the window document factual hallucinations in contemporary chatbots, including systems given retrieved context. Nothing shows that fabrication was reliably eliminated. The mitigations in e2 reduce the risk but do not remove it, so the claim holds on the contract's plain reading.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The two parts are kept together: ChatGPT uses facts unreliably and has no explicit, stable internal model. No version is named.

contract.note: Treating the two parts separately and requiring evidence on internal representation for the second is fair. The June window is an evaluator convention.

evidence.note: OpenAI SimpleQA (Oct 2024) documents hallucinations on a deliberately hard benchmark. It predates the window and says nothing about internal models.

o3/o4-mini system card (April 2025) shows factual errors on questions about people. It is outside the June window, does not identify the ChatGPT configuration, and does not test internal representation.

reviews.rationale: The packet's evidence predates the window and only addresses factual errors in general. It does not show unreliable use of well-documented facts in June 2025 ChatGPT, and nothing addresses whether ChatGPT lacks an explicit, stable internal model. The packet's own stated gaps say this. Neither part is settled.
